title: Resetting the Login Credentials or MFA

blocks.text: You can reset the password or multi-factor authentication (MFA) when you've forgotten the credentials or when required.

blocks.item: On the login page, enter your Login ID, then click Next.
On the next page, click Having trouble logging in?
The link to reset the password is sent to your email address. This link remains valid for 15 minutes. After 15 minutes, you need to resend the link again.
Open the email and click the link. You must verify with the registered MFA option for resetting a password.
On the second-factor authentication page, enter details for authentication type and click Verify. You can reset the password after successful verification.
Confirm New Password: Re-enter the password to confirm.
Click Re-Login to log in to Zscaler Admin Console.
To reset the password by requesting another administrator, see Configuring Security Settings for Users.

If you cannot use a configured MFA method in certain scenarios (e.g., using a new device), inform another Authentication Service administrator to reset the MFA methods for your user account. An administrator might delete the configured MFA option from the Security Settings section for your user account. You are then prompted to reconfigure MFA the next time you log in to Zscaler Admin Console.
To reset a user's MFA as an administrator:
From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Authentication > Users.
Click the Edit icon for the affected user.
Delete all the MFA methods configured for the user, such as time-based one-time password (TOTP), Email OTP, or Fast Identity Online (FIDO), and click Save.
Sign in to Zscaler Admin Console and configure the MFA again.
Sign in again to Zscaler Admin Console with the newly configured MFA method and confirm that the login is successful.
If the user requests you to reset their password, see the Resetting Password section.
Administrators can also delete the Email OTP option for users who have chosen it as an MFA method.
